summary: The note describes a new national cybersecurity strategy unveiled by Minister of National Security Alex Richards to protect critical national infrastructure (CNI) such as energy grids, transport and communications. It rests on risk management, public-private collaboration, workforce training, incident response and cyber hygiene, and was prompted by a surge in attacks including a December 2023 energy sector attack that caused blackouts.
one_line: A national cybersecurity strategy unveiled in October 2023 aims to protect critical infrastructure through risk management, public-private collaboration, workforce training, incident response, and cyber hygiene.
key_facts: Minister of National Security Alex Richards unveiled the national cybersecurity strategy on October 17, 2023.
On December 5, 2023, the country suffered an unprecedented cyber-attack on its energy sector that caused temporary blackouts in several cities.
The International Cybersecurity Protection Alliance reports a 300% increase in cyber-attacks on national infrastructure systems worldwide over the last year.
The strategy centers on a Risk Management Framework (RMF) that standardizes identifying, assessing, and responding to cyber risks.
The RMF uses a tiered approach: strategic decisions at the highest level align cybersecurity with national objectives, while infrastructure operators integrate risk management into operations.
On September 21, 2023, the government rolled out voluntary guidelines for private companies to strengthen their security postures and align with federal initiatives.
The strategy calls for more government-private sector collaboration because much of the national infrastructure is privately owned and operated.
The National Cybersecurity Training Center opened on November 10, 2023, to address the cybersecurity workforce skills gap.
The incident response guidelines cover early detection of breaches, swift containment of threats, and system restoration.
The country has run several cyber incident simulations with international partners to prepare response teams across agencies and companies.
Cyber hygiene practices include regular software updates, strong authentication protocols, employee awareness training, and sector-tailored best practices.
Dr. Martin Hayes, CISO of the National Cybersecurity Agency, said cyber hygiene "forms the first line of defense and can turn away the majority of cyber threats."
Cybersecurity expert Emily Thompson stressed that public and private sectors must work in unison, with government sharing intelligence and resources.
